text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - The German Bund market received a welcome tonic as U.S. credit markets reacted positively to benign confidence and inflation indicators. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.04, up 0/63 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended 10/32 higher after a quiet session as traders awaited a raft of U.S. data due this week and Thursday's British election. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-24/32, up 22/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - The June bond future settled at the highest level since April 17 after weak U.S. data sparked rallies in major bond markets, PIBOR was also buoyed, the franc slipped from highs as the dollar lost some ground vs mark. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.90, up 0.58 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and BTP futures ended at the day's highs, boosted by a general rally on other debt markets in line with firmer T-bonds after a raft of market-friendly U.S. data. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.12, up 0.42 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were higher in mid-morning trade after the Conference Board reported a "not worrisome" dip in the April consumer confidence index to 116.8 from March's 118.5. with early gains scored on softer than expected first-quarter employment costs. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-24/32, up 1/11/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.00 percent.

JAPAN - Japan's financial markets were closed for a National Holiday and will reopen on Wednesday. In after-hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.58, up 0.37 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - The primary market kicked off with a $1.5 billion five-year floating rate note for Italy. Joint lead managers for the transaction are HSBC and Lehman Brothers.
Lehman Brothers was also the joint lead manager on a $2 billion five-year FRN launched last July, though Tuesday's deal was priced around 10 basis points tighter.
